$description: Thermal time constants (tau, minutes) for cold compartments, anchored to USDA power-outage guidance. These are defaults; a household's own measured events override them (TH-07).

reference.notes: tau values derived so the RC model T(t)=T_amb+(T_0-T_amb)e^(-t/tau) reproduces USDA rules of thumb at the reference ambient. USDA FSIS 'Power Outages & Food Safety': a refrigerator keeps food safe for up to about 4 h; a full freezer holds about 48 h; a half-full freezer about 24 h; refrigerated food must stay at 40 F (4.4 C) or below. v2 corrects the refrigerated danger threshold from 5 C to 4.4 C (40 F), the USDA figure and the more conservative choice. Content rephrased for compliance.

derivation.fridge: Start 3C, ambient 22C, perishable danger 4.4C (40F). Reaching 4.4C in 240 min => tau = -240 / ln((22-4.4)/(22-3)) ~= 3136 min.
derivation.freezerFull: Start -18C, ambient 22C, frozen-danger 0C (ice crystals rule). Reaching 0C in 2880 min (48 h) => tau = -2880 / ln((22-0)/(22-(-18))) = -2880 / ln(22/40) ~= 4815 min.
derivation.freezerHalf: Same bounds, reaching 0C in 1440 min (24 h) => tau = -1440 / ln(22/40) ~= 2408 min.
